name: Sodium beta-hydroxybutyrate (BHB salts)
lead: Sodium beta-hydroxybutyrate is a salt form of beta-hydroxybutyrate (BHB), the main ketone body the liver makes during fasting, prolonged exercise and low-carbohydrate diets. [1][2] In supplements, BHB is bound to sodium, potassium, magnesium or calcium; most products are racemic, so only about half is the biologically used D form. [3]
Sellers market ketone salts as a way to raise blood ketones without dietary restriction, with claims about appetite, energy and fat loss. [3] These claims are commonly discussed in fat-loss contexts.

Human studies of BHB administration are mostly small physiology trials in healthy people and in patients with diabetes or heart failure; none located in the sources reviewed tests BHB salts for fat loss or appearance.

paras: Ketone bodies are produced by the liver and used by tissues when glucose is scarce; the two main ones are acetoacetate and beta-hydroxybutyrate. [2] Classic studies showed that during prolonged starvation the brain uses ketone bodies in place of much of its glucose. [4][5] Reviews have discussed ketone bodies in ketogenic diets, insulin resistance and mitochondrial metabolism. [6]
Salts slightly raise blood pH, whereas esters lower it, according to Wikipedia. [3] The most-studied ester is a separate compound, described in its own entry.

Registered studies of exogenous ketosis include safety and tolerability of free BHB, effects on kidney function, cognition during exercise-heat stress, brain ketone metabolism in type 1 diabetes, a BHB ester in ALS, BHB in type 1 and type 2 diabetes, and nutritional ketosis in heart failure. [7][8][9][10][11][12][13] Several of these use esters or free BHB rather than salts. No studies found testing sodium BHB salts specifically for fat loss or appearance.

card.summary: Ketone-salt supplements raise blood BHB; fat-loss and looks claims have not been tested.
card.note: Sodium load; many products are racemic.

quick.overview:
BHB salts are supplements that bind the ketone beta-hydroxybutyrate to minerals such as sodium. They are sold to raise blood ketones without fasting or a ketogenic diet.

Research is limited to small physiology studies, and fat loss from the salts has not been shown in published trials found here.
quick.mechanism: BHB is a fuel the body makes during fasting and uses in the brain and muscle. Salts supply it directly, though racemic products contain a form that is less used.
quick.risks: Salts add a mineral load (such as sodium) and slightly raise blood pH. Long-term safety data in healthy dieters are limited.
